equity_bridge.item: Killara Feedlot sale proceeds, net of estimated tax and costs
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 note 15: agreed 25 Feb 2026 with Australian Meat Group for ~A$195.8m, subject to FIRB and ACCC, completion expected before 30 June 2026. Net assets held for sale A$118.0m, so a ~A$78m gain; A$175m allows ~A$21m for tax and transaction costs. Killara is excluded from the continuing-operations revenue and margin base, so its value enters here (matching-asset rule). COMPLETION NOT VERIFIED from a filing - if the sale lapsed, remove this line and add ~A$190m of revenue at ~7% EBIT margin back to the flows.
A$4.6m FY2025 NCI profit share x ~11; see nci_treatment

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: organic revenue growth for a mature distributor; equity CAGR rejected (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (8-10%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (3yr -2.4%) and statutory EPS (3yr -36%, 5yr -19%). Equity grew through share issuance - A$245.8m raised in FY2025 and A$155.0m of scrip to Delta vendors in FY2026, shares on issue up from 155m (FY2020) to 214m - not through retained earnings; equity per share compounded ~6% over five years. Shareholders' equity also includes non-controlling interests. Equity CAGR is therefore not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 annual is the end point; FY2022 and FY2020 are the start points. The FCF series is lease-adjusted owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - lease principal - SBC: FY2020 A$99.7m, FY2022 A$49.0m, FY2025 A$23.3m (84.7 - 60.5 - 0.8). inputs.reported_fcf of A$24.1m is the FY2025 figure after lease principal, so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - SBC holds. This series is after interest paid and includes Killara, and it swings with working capital (FY2023 +A$121m, FY2018/FY2019 negative), so its CAGR is a weak signal. SBC is immaterial, so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF growth are effectively the same. EPS is statutory diluted; underlying EPS was 97.3c (FY2022) and 46.5c (FY2025), a 3yr CAGR of -21.8%. FY2016-FY2018 include operations later discontinued and are not used.

scenario_narratives.base: Delta is integrated without drama: a full twelve months of ownership in FY2027 and the first procurement synergies roughly offset the softer 2026-27 season ABARES forecasts (production value down ~5%, cattle and sheep prices lower). Organic sales grow 3-3.5% a year, broadly rural-input inflation plus modest share gain, fading to 2.5%. Underlying EBIT margin moves from ~4.5% to ~5.0% as Systems Modernisation costs roll off and backward integration (AgriToll, Titan Ag) and Delta synergies come through over three years - the middle of the last six years' range, not the FY2021-FY2022 peak. Return on capital stays below the 15% target. Leverage falls through Killara proceeds and retained cash, with no equity raise.
scenario_narratives.bull: A run of good seasons coincides with the Delta synergy window. Crop-protection and fertiliser volumes recover in South Australia and Victoria, livestock and wool prices hold, and rate cuts keep Real Estate and the Elders Finance broker model growing. Elders uses its ~324-site network to take share from independents, and backward integration lifts retail gross margin. Underlying EBIT margin returns to ~5.9%, in line with FY2020-FY2022, and stays there because the mix has shifted toward agency, real estate and financial services. Working capital efficiency improves on the new Dynamics 365 retail system.
scenario_narratives.bear: The drier 2026-27 season becomes a multi-year drought while leverage is still elevated. Sales fall 5% in FY2027 and stall the year after; localised price competition from Nutrien in crop protection compresses retail margin; Delta synergies are slower under a new external CEO in his first year. Underlying EBIT margin drops to ~3.6% (below the FY2024 trough of 4.1%, on a lower-margin post-Delta mix) and recovers only to ~4.4%. The working-capital release from lower sales cushions cash flow, but with leverage starting at 3.8x there is a real chance of a dilutive equity raise that this scenario's flat share count does not model - the bear value is therefore not a floor.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Elders is valued as a cyclical, working-capital-heavy distributor on mid-cycle margins, not on the acquisition-assisted growth target management quotes. The valuation is built on an estimated FY2026 pro forma base because the business changed shape after the last annual report (Delta in, Killara out); leases are charged as an operating cost and kept out of net debt; minorities and the Killara proceeds are handled once each in the bridge. The terminal multiple is capped at 14x free cash flow in the base case, which binds ahead of the Gordon value.
key_risks_to_valuation: The FY2026 base (revenue A$4,030m, underlying EBIT ~A$180m) is an estimate; the FY2026 result, due around mid-November 2026, will replace it and may move year-1 drivers materially
Net debt is as at 31 March 2026 and excludes second-half cash flow; March and September working capital differ seasonally
Killara Feedlot proceeds (A$175m net, ~A$0.82 per share) are included on the assumption the sale completed; this was not verified from a filing
A 0.5pp change in the mature EBIT margin moves base value by roughly a fifth - the valuation is a margin call on a ~5% margin business
Leverage: an equity raise in a downturn would dilute below the modelled bear value
Organic-only growth: if Elders keeps buying bolt-ons, both growth and cash outflow will be higher than modelled

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4.96-7.77
data_sources.financials: ELD.AX_Metrics.csv (FY2016-FY2025, H1 FY2026); ELD.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt for the 31 March 2026 balance sheet, borrowings (note 8), share capital (note 9), Delta acquisition (note 14) and Killara (note 15); ELD.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt for D&A split, lease interest and tax losses

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow statement share-based payment add-back (A$0.8m); no equity-award tax line exists (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in every period). History ranges A$-0.4m to A$3.6m, so the forward charge is set at 0.05% of revenue rather than the unusually low FY2025 print.
inputs.share_count_basis: 214.48m ordinary shares on issue at 31 March 2026 (H1 FY2026 note 9: 191.21m opening + 22.30m issued to Delta vendors at A$6.95 + 0.97m DRP). Diluted weighted average equals basic in the filing, so there are no dilutive securities to add. Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows; DRP issuance replaces a cash dividend at market price and is treated as value-neutral.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ended 30 Sep 2026, continuing operations, pro forma estimate - not yet reported)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in AUD: risk-free ~4.4% (Australian 10-year government bond), equity risk premium ~5.75%, beta ~1.05 for a cyclical rural-services distributor gives cost of equity ~10.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6% (4.2% after 30% tax). Borrowings of A$622m net against ~A$1.4bn market capitalisation is ~30% debt, giving ~8.6%; 8.5% used. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios - cyclicality and leverage risk are charged in the flows and the scenario weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as an operating cost. The full lease payment (principal + interest, FY2025 A$60.5m + A$5.7m = 2.07% of revenue; H1 FY2026 A$33.3m + A$3.5m = 2.08%) is deducted via lease_cost_pct_path at 1.9% of the larger post-Delta revenue base (Delta brought only A$14.8m of lease liabilities on ~A$850m of sales). Lease liabilities of A$279.4m are EXCLUDED from net debt: net_debt A$621.6m is borrowings A$709.1m less cash A$87.5m, versus the company's own A$901.0m which includes leases. D&A is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 A$21.3m of the A$83.6m total). EBITDA margin is therefore the post-AASB 16 underlying figure.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge. Flows are 100% consolidated; non-controlling partners take A$4.6-5.0m of profit a year (FY2023-FY2025) and A$3.8m of distributions per half, capitalised at ~11x to A$50m and deducted in equity_bridge. Book NCI is only A$2.9m, which would understate the claim.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (routing row 2 of dcf-methods). Elders is an operating distributor and agency business, not a lender - debtor interest (A$15.9m FY2025) is trade-credit income inside operating revenue and its receivables funding sits in borrowings. NET DEBT, NOT NET CASH: no interest-income strip. FY0 CHOICE: the latest ANNUAL filing is FY2025 (September 2025) but the Delta Agribusiness acquisition completed 3 November 2025 and the Killara Feedlot is held for sale, so FY2025 is not a usable base. base_revenue is a pro forma FY2026E continuing-operations estimate of A$4,030m = H1 FY2026 actual A$1,767.7m (incl. five months of Delta at A$348.0m) + H2 legacy ~A$1,780m (H2 FY2025 continuing ~A$1,710m grown ~4%, against +5.8% in H1) + H2 Delta ~A$480m (Delta sales are second-half weighted). Year 1 of the projection is FY2027. FY2026 full-year results had not been released in the extracted filings at the valuation date (Elders reported FY2025 on 17 November 2025), so every FY2026 figure here is an estimate that should be replaced on the result. ANCHORS: net debt and shares are from the 31 March 2026 half-year balance sheet, the latest filed; cash flow between April and September 2026 is not captured. WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture is negative (-18%) because receivables + inventory exceed payables (A$803.6m working capital on ~A$4.0bn of sales); growth consumes cash and a revenue fall releases it. ACQUISITIONS: Elders has historically bought A$30-60m of bolt-ons a year; the growth paths here are organic only and no acquisition spend is charged, so they must not be read against the company's 5-10% EBIT growth target, which is acquisition-assisted. BUYBACKS: none (A$0.1m purchased for employee schemes in H1 FY2026); the flat count is a modelling convention. HOUSE/STREET: SBC is ~0.05% of revenue so the two bases are within a few cents; the band is not informative for this name. UNDERLYING vs STATUTORY: margins are anchored on underlying EBIT (FY2025 A$143.5m incl. Killara; H1 FY2026 A$76.6m continuing) with a deduction in years 1-2 for the Systems Modernisation and integration costs management excludes (FY2025 statutory NPAT A$50.3m vs underlying A$86.0m).

base.margin_note: ebitda_margin is post-AASB 16 underlying EBITDA. Underlying EBIT margin = ebitda_margin - 0.8 (D&A ex right-of-use) - ~1.72 (right-of-use depreciation, approximated by lease principal). Year 1 (FY2027) implies ~4.6% underlying EBIT less ~0.15pp of excluded transformation costs, against ~4.5% estimated for FY2026 and 4.5% reported for FY2025; the path matures at ~5.0%, the middle of the FY2020-FY2025 range of 4.1-6.7%.
base.tax_note: Booked tax losses were fully utilised in FY2025 (carried-forward value nil, FY2025 AR note 3), so the A$3-9m a year of cash tax paid historically is not repeatable. Ramps to the 30% Australian statutory rate by year 3; years 1-2 allow for payment timing.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25%: leverage of 3.8x at March 2026 heading into a forecast weaker season, a receivables facility that rolls in December 2026, and a CEO change during integration. Base 50%: the margin path needs only a return to the middle of the recent range. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs favourable seasons, full Delta synergies and a sustained margin near the last cycle's peak at the same time, and return on capital has run below target for years.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
